summary: Lemma3.2 lacks initial-peak dependence and the Neumann quadratic-form identity omits k2=0 weight. Data-dependent iteration restores qualitative conditional regularity; weight repair is a bounded constant factor. Energy sign and terminal level accounting consistent within scope.

problems.title: Uniform initial-time Linfinity estimate does not follow from L2 alone
problems.claim: If ||rho-rho_M||_2<=2M on [0,T], M>=max(1,sqrt(rho_M)), then ||rho-rho_M||_infinity<=C M^2 with universal C, including t=0.
assumptions_checked: rho0,A=A phi(A(x-x*)), phi smooth compactly supported in unit disk,0<=phi<=1,phi0=1,x*=(0,pi/2),A>=1.
Support away from boundaries/periodic seam, so smooth nonnegative compatible data.
L2 squared<=pi<4 and mean<=1/(2pi A); local continuity gives short interval satisfying premise with M1 and any fixed nonzero g.
problems.decisive_check: Initial centered peak>=A-1/(2pi A)->infinity, contradicting universal C.
problems.core_dependency: Printed Lemma3.2 quantitative bound used to infer bounded-L2 conditional regularity in Corollary3.3.
problems.impact_rationale: Minor: independent Lp/Nash iteration with initial-peak dependence proves the finite bound actually required for fixed initial data. No singular solution or main-theorem counterexample.
problems.repair_candidate: Retain dependence on initial L^infinity. With K=sup ||rho||_2, Y_p'+||grad(rho^(p/2))||_2^2<=C p^2(1+K^2)Y_p. Nash gives A_p<=max(||rho_0||_p,[C p^2(1+K^2)]^(1/p) A_(p/2)); dyadic products converge.
problems.repair_boundary: Qualitative implication restored for regular nonnegative solutions under the stated boundaries; the universal C M^2 formula at t=0 is not restored. Local existence is taken from the stated source theorem, not independently reconstructed.
counterevidence: The L2 hypothesis holds for an actual short solution interval, not just arbitrary non-solution functions.
The example obeys boundary and nonnegativity assumptions.
A data-dependent bound suffices for the downstream finite-time blowup contradiction.

problems.title: Neumann Parseval identity omits zero-vertical-mode weight
problems.claim: Under the stated Fourier normalization, the gradient norm squared is asserted equal to the unweighted sum of |k|^2 |fhat_N(k)|^2.
assumptions_checked: f=cos x1 is smooth, meanzero, Neumann and equals horizontal fluctuation.
problems.decisive_check: For f=cos(x_1), integral |grad f|^2 = pi^2, while the unweighted coefficient sum is 2 pi^2. The exact quadratic form divides each term by 1+delta_(k2,0).
problems.core_dependency: Quadratic-form/Parseval bookkeeping in Fourier cone estimates.
problems.impact_rationale: Minor: missing weights stay between1/2 and1; corrected estimates retain universal constants after auxiliary-parameter adjustment.
problems.repair_candidate: Insert1/(1+delta_(k2,0)) into L2 and gradient Parseval sums or switch consistently to orthonormal coefficients.
problems.repair_boundary: Normalization repair exact; full lattice-counting/cone-transfer proof not certified.
counterevidence: This is a zero vertical mode, not the excluded zero horizontal fluctuation.
Nonzero vertical modes have weight1; discrepancy is localized.

issue_results.source_location: arXiv 2305.01036v2, Lemma 3.2 and Corollary 3.3, physical/printed p.9; local existence p.7; full system p.4
issue_results.source_claim_verified: The native p.9 image states a universal C M^2 bound under a bound on [0,T], without dependence on the initial peak; p.6 explicitly defines C as a universal domain constant.
issue_results.assumptions_verified: For any fixed nonzero g, rho_0,A=A phi(A(x-x_*)), with 0<=phi<=1 smooth in the unit disk and phi(0)=1, is periodic-compatible, nonnegative and has zero normal derivative since its support is interior. The two-dimensional change of variables gives centered L2 norm squared <=pi<4 and rho_M<=1/(2pi A)<1. Local existence and continuity therefore supply a positive short interval with the exact premise M=1.
issue_results.decisive_evidence: At t=0 the centered supremum is at least A-1/(2pi A), unbounded as A increases. The universal constant claimed in Lemma 3.2 cannot exist.
issue_results.repair_verification: Independently checked the report's test by rho^(p-1), cancellation of divergence-free advection and boundary fluxes, the chemotaxis term (p-1) integral rho^(p+1)-(p-1)rho_M Y_p, the two-dimensional L4 interpolation, Young absorption, and Nash logistic barrier. Dyadic iteration retains initial L-infinity dependence and gives a finite bound when K=sup ||rho||_2 is finite. The zero-density case needs no division.
issue_results.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The quantitative initial-time bound is stronger than the actual downstream requirement. Corollary 3.3 needs finiteness for a fixed smooth datum, which the independently checked data-dependent iteration supplies. The Riccati argument then has the correct backward inequality. No critical-regularity mechanism is refuted by these spikes.
issue_results.severity_reason: Minor is retained because the demonstrated false part is data-uniform initial-time control, while the precise qualitative implication used in the main proof survives with a verified bound. This is a scope determination, not a downgrade based only on repair difficulty or survival of unrelated results.
issue_results.version_limit: All claims are about the acquired v2; journal-final equivalence remains unestablished.

issue_results.source_claim_verified: The inverse Neumann expansion includes 1/(1+delta(k2)), but the displayed quadratic form omits that weight. Native p.7 inspection confirms the discrepancy.
issue_results.assumptions_verified: f=cos(x1) is a real smooth periodic function, Neumann in x2, mean zero, and has zero horizontal mean. Thus its k2=0 term is not removed by the horizontal-fluctuation convention.
issue_results.decisive_evidence: The coefficients at (+/-1,0) each equal pi; direct integration gives ||grad f||_2^2=pi^2, whereas the printed sum gives 2pi^2. Orthogonality of cos(k2 x2) yields the required denominator 1+delta(k2).
issue_results.repair_verification: The corrected L2 and gradient forms have weights in [1/2,1]. Read the uses in (6.7)-(6.9): the small cone parameter a may be reduced so the complementary mass is absorbed after a bounded-factor change, leaving the same power of N and lambda and universal constants. No full reproof of the cone transfer is claimed.
issue_results.severity_reason: The identity is false as printed but the discrepancy is a uniform norm-equivalence factor; no failure of the cone estimate's scaling or core conclusion is established.

corrections: Restored missing squared-power notation in the current findings from the unchanged report/source formulas; both Minor findings and report text retained.
